newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - Soul searching begins at North Harbour.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Soul searching begins at North Harbour.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Sept 17 - The North Harbour Knights will begin an intense period of soul searching when they regroup for the first time on Wednesday since their Ranfurly Shield rugby loss to Waikato last Friday, NZPA reports.
Harbour have been labelled "chokers" in the aftermath of their 17-14 loss to the shield holders.
Harbour have much work ahead if they are to restore lost pride in a so far ragged National Provincial Championship (NPC) campaign, which hasn't been helped by two shield challenges.
With All Blacks centre Frank Bunce out for at least another week following a knock to the head in the shield challenge, things haven't improved for Harbour over the weekend.

"We're not diving, we're not hiding, there is no doubt about it that we, particularly the coaching staff, are extremely disappointed with what happened last Friday night," coach Brad Meurant said today.
"I think the criticism from our supporters and the disappointment they feel is well founded, we haven't produced the goods yet.
"I'm not criticising my players but I feel there were critical aspects of the decision-making on field that weren't correct.
"So obviously we now need to sit down and do some serious soul searching about where we want to go, what we want to achieve and whether we are determined enough to do it from here."
Meurant said there were other poorly performing teams in the NPC who weren't subject to the same criticism. There have been calls for Meurant's head and the sacking of key players.
"You just never win do you? We played well against Wellington and we were the flavour of the week, we didn't against Waikato and it's the end of the world," he said.
"It is not the end of the world even if we have to seriously start shaping up now."
He said he didn't think All Blacks lock Ian Jones had come back a week too soon from a knee injury incurred in South Africa.

"It didn't look good that his opposite took all the lineout ball, but with the way the lineouts are these days you would have to expect good locks like Mark Cooksley to do just what he did," Meurant said.
"I don't think anyone can criticise Ian, we just never had the ball to put in and when we did he did the job we asked of him."
Despite the poor Harbour performance, Meurant isn't likely to make sweeping changes ahead of next Sunday's game against Counties at Takapuna.

"Before you do that you have to see if you have the depth and whether there is anything to be achieved by it. We will look at our playing personnel but there won't be wholesale slaughter unless there is purpose to it," he said.
The Harbour team will be named tomorrow night.
